text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday, prepared for Reuters by the Estonian news agency, ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Workers of the bankrupt Oru peat plant who were paid not two but only one month's wages, took Avo Blankin, chairman of the local city council as hostage although he was freed the same day unhurt.
- The prevailing opinion in parliament is that the report of the Bank of Estonia should be disclosed to the public, Daimar Liiv, chairman of the parliamentary legal commission, said.
- The Reform Party and the Tartu 2000 union plan to set up a minority government in the southern town of Tartu with Roman Mugur as probable candidate for mayor.
- The second reading of the draft law, abolishing the death sentence, was suspended in parliament.
- Estonia is not prepared to restart border negotiations with Russia because the agreement is ready for signing, Prime Minister Mart Siimann told journalists.

- Arnold Ruutel, who held the post of the chairman of the Supreme Council in the period of restoration of independence, was allocated 475,400 kroons by the government under the law that determines the privileges of ex-presidents.
- Tallinna Kaubamaja said the first day of its Helsinki shop was more successful than expected, the management said.
- The Bank of Estonia had a record profit of 186.6 million kroons in 1996.
- Italian businessman Ernesto Preatoni, who has invested 600 million kroons in Estonia in the last two years, recommends the country not to hurry to join the European Union.
